mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to expected equity cash flows, increasing the present value of future dividends and earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals tightening monetary policy, which raises the cost of capital and compresses discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 2% month-over-month indicates labor market weakness, which reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in rising claims periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 1% month-over-month signals strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in falling claims periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 106.3127 over 3 months indicates weakening domestic demand, which compresses corporate earnings growth and reduces equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in declining production periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in residential construction (HOUST) above 1739.0 units indicates strengthening domestic demand for housing, which supports economic growth and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rising construction periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 266.832 over 3 months signals disinflation, which reduces the risk premium on equity valuations and supports higher forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in disinflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above 619923.0 million dollars indicates stronger consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rising sales periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
